headline: US PCE Inflation Accelerates to 3.6% YTD as September Index Rises 0.5%
summary: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose 0.5% in September, pushing year-to-date inflation to 3.6%. Personal income increased $54.5 billion while consumer spending rose by $113.1 billion during the month.
why: The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index is the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, directly influencing monetary policy decisions.

impacts.name: US Dollar
impacts.why: Higher inflation reduces expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts, strengthening the currency.

why_moved: Accelerating inflation data reduces the likelihood of monetary easing by the Federal Reserve, weighing on asset valuations.
